Yes. HTTP/3 runs over QUIC (RFC 9000), and QUIC runs over UDP. QUIC supplies its own reliability, congestion control, stream multiplexing, and TLS 1.3 encryption in user space, so UDP serves mainly as a transport substrate that traverses existing middleboxes.

Caveat: some networks block or throttle UDP/443, so clients typically fall back to HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 over TCP, discovered via the `Alt-Svc` header or HTTPS DNS records.
